records.quote: Counterexample 3.1. Let, Xi ∼ Kw-G(x, αi, γi; G) and Yi ∼ Kw-G(x, βi, γi; H), for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Set (γ1,...,γ5) = (1.2, 1.5, 1.9, 2, 2.1), (α1,...,α5) = (1.1, 0.001, 0.0001, 0.00001, 0.00001) and (β1,...,β5) = (2.1, 3.001, 5.0001, 0.001, 0.0001). Clearly, (α1,...,α5) ⪰w (β1,...,β5). Let G(x) = e^{−1/x} and H(x) = 1−e^{−x}, for x > 0. Also, let (X1,X2,X3) be selected with probability P(N1 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (X1,...,X4) with probability P(N1 = 4) = p(4) = 2/5 and (X1,...,X5) with probability P(N1 = 5) = p(5) = 2/5; further let (Y1,Y2,Y3) with P(N2 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (Y1,...,Y4) with P(N2 = 4) = p(4) = 3/5 and (Y1,...,Y5) with P(N2 = 5) = p(5) = 1/5. Here, N1 ≤st N2. Let us use the Gumbel copula with generators ψ1(x) = e^{−x^{1/a}} and ψ2(x) = e^{−x^{1/b}}, x > 0, with a = 2 and b = 2.1. Clearly, all the conditions are satisfied except ψ1 and ψ2 are log-concave. Figure 1(a) displays that the difference between F_{X_{N1:N1}}(x) and F_{Y_{N2:N2}}(x) crosses x axis, which violates the result in Theorem 3.1.
records.model: other: random maxima X_{N1:N1}, Y_{N2:N2} with random sample sizes N1, N2 under Archimedean copulas
records.family: Kw-G(x, αi, γi; G) vs Kw-G(x, βi, γi; H); G(x)=e^{−1/x}, H(x)=1−e^{−x}; Gumbel generators ψ1(x)=e^{−x^{1/a}}, ψ2(x)=e^{−x^{1/b}}
records.compared: α ⪰w β with common γ; baseline G vs H; random counts N1 <=st N2

hypotheses.text: all the conditions [of Theorem 3.1] are satisfied except ψ1 and ψ2 are log-concave

conclusion.direction: refutes Theorem 3.1: the claimed X_{N1:N1} >=st Y_{N2:N2} fails — F difference crosses the x axis

records.ambiguity: Body says 'difference between F_XN1:N1(x) and F_YN2:N2(x)'; Figure 1(a) caption says the plotted difference is in survival functions F̄ — either way a sign change violates the st conclusion.

note: Counterexample refutes Theorem 3.1's X_{N1:N1} >=st Y_{N2:N2} by a sign-changing difference; record states the refuted direction (A's framing, B's 'neither' normalized differently).

records.quote: Counterexample 3.2. Let, Xi ∼ Kw-G(x, αi, γi; G) and Yi ∼ Kw-G(x, αi, δi; H), for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Further, let (γ1,...,γ5) = (3.9, 3.1, 2.9, 2.8, 2.1), (δ1,...,δ5) = (3.2, 2.6, 1.9, 1.2, 1) and (α1,...,α5) = (β1,...,β5) = (0.01, 7, 9, 9.1, 9.12). Clearly, (γ1,...,γ5) ⪰w (δ1,...,δ5). Let G(x) = e^{−1/x} and H(x) = 1 − e^{−x}, for x > 0. Also, let (X1,X2,X3) be selected with probability P(N1 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (X1,...,X4) with P(N1 = 4) = p(4) = 2/5 and (X1,...,X5) with P(N1 = 5) = p(5) = 2/5; further let (Y1,Y2,Y3) with P(N2 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (Y1,...,Y4) with P(N2 = 4) = p(4) = 3/5 and (Y1,...,Y5) with P(N2 = 5) = p(5) = 1/5. Here, N1 ≤st N2. Consider the Gumbel copula with generators ψ1(x) = e^{−x^{1/a}} and ψ2(x) = e^{−x^{1/b}}, x > 0, with a = 1.4 and b = 2.5. Here, all the conditions of Theorem 3.3 are satisfied except G ≥ H. Figure 1(b) displays the difference between F̄_{X_{1:N1}}(x) and F̄_{Y_{1:N2}}(x) crosses x axis for some x ≥ 0, which violates the statement of Theorem 3.3.

records.quote: Counterexample 3.3. Suppose Xi ∼ Kw-G(x, αi, γi; G) and Yi ∼ Kw-G(x, αi, δi; H), for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Further, let (α1,...,α5) = (7.1, 2.9, 1.56, 0.03, 0.201), (β1,...,β5) = (8.1, 3.009, 2.6, 1.06, 0.01) and (γ1,...,γ5) = (δ1,...,δ5) = (5.02, 2.05, 1.09, 0.01, 0.001). It is easy to see that (α1,...,α5) ⪰w (β1,...,β5). Let H(x) = e^{−1/x} and G(x) = 1 − e^{−x}, for x > 0. Also, let (X1,X2,X3) be selected with probability P(N1 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (X1,...,X4) with P(N1 = 4) = p(4) = 2/5 and (X1,...,X5) with P(N1 = 5) = p(5) = 2/5; further, let (Y1,Y2,Y3) with P(N2 = 3) = p(3) = 1/5, (Y1,...,Y4) with P(N2 = 4) = p(4) = 3/5 and (Y1,...,Y5) with P(N2 = 5) = p(5) = 1/5, which satisfy the condition N1 ≤st N2. Choose the Gumbel-Hougaard copula with generators ψ1(x) = e^{1−(1+x)^{1/a}} and ψ2(x) = e^{1−(1+x)^{1/b}}, x > 0, with a = 4.0002 and b = 4.0001. So, all the conditions of Theorem 3.4 are satisfied except the log-convexity of ψ1 and ψ2. Figure 2 displays the difference between F̄_{X_{1:N1}}(x) and F̄_{Y_{1:N2}}(x) crosses x axis for some x ≥ 0. Therefore, Theorem 3.4 can not be possible without the log-convexity property of the generators.
